PREMISE FALSIFIED by the filer. Read this before planning anything. #2546 arm 2 P5 DOES use GPU; my no-CUDA-context claim was a bad inference from a too-short window.

## The falsifying observation

A later poll tick on the SAME phase, same pod, same run:

    gpu_util = 52,0,70,0

GPUs 0 and 2 at 52 percent and 70 percent. So the phase allocates CUDA contexts and does real GPU
work. The task body's central claim — that P5 ran a 4xH100 pod with no CUDA context at all — is
WRONG.

## What I actually measured, and where the inference broke

The measurement was real: 8 nvidia-smi samples over 56 s, all four GPUs at 0 percent AND 0 MiB.
The error was treating that as a property of the PHASE rather than of the 56 seconds.

P5 fans out 71 registry jobs across 4 work-conserving workers over a ~2h phase. The jobs are
heterogeneous. My window landed in a CPU-only stretch. Nothing about 0 MiB at time T constrains
time T plus 40 minutes.

The epistemic asymmetry I got backwards, stated so the next reader does not repeat it: a ZERO
utilization reading is WEAK evidence, because it only reports absence during the sampled window. A
NONZERO reading is STRONG evidence, because 52 percent and 70 percent cannot be a sampling
artifact. I leaned on a window of zeros as though it were strong, and I even reported it as
conclusive on the grounds that 0 MiB rules out sampling between kernels. That reasoning is valid
only within the window.

## What survives, and what does not

DOES NOT SURVIVE:
  - the claim that P5 allocates no CUDA context
  - the claim that P5 is a CPU-only phase mis-routed to a GPU lane
  - the framing that the plan made a wrong lane call
  - the title of this task

MAY STILL SURVIVE, but is a much weaker and different task than what I filed:
  - the poller posted a gpu-idle advisory (all 4 GPUs idle 30 min during healthy phase=p5_fits)
    on a phase that legitimately alternates between CPU-only and GPU-using jobs. So the question
    of whether a 30-minute idle window is meaningful for a HETEROGENEOUS phase is real, but it is
    an advisory-tuning question, not a missing-verification question.
  - the general point that nothing cross-checks a plan's GPU-worthiness claim against realized use
    is still true. But my motivating example is gone, so the task no longer has a demonstrated
    instance, and a workflow change with no demonstrated instance is worth much less.

## Recommendation from the filer

Do NOT implement the check as scoped. Either narrow this to the advisory-tuning question above
with the corrected facts, or close it as premise-falsified and let the general point wait for an
instance that actually holds up. That call belongs to this task's planner, not to me, but planning
against the body as written would be building on a claim I have just retracted.

Whoever picks this up: the parent #2546 correction is posted there too, so the two records agree.

Do NOT touch the live #2546 arm-2 pod.

Addendum to the premise-falsified note: the refined signature is directly useful for the ONE surviving question, so here it is precisely.

20 samples over 200 s on the same phase:

    gpu 0   0 %   38,711 MiB      compute app 54990   38,702 MiB
    gpu 1   0 %   48,173 MiB      compute app 54991   48,164 MiB
    gpu 2   0 %   51,561 MiB      compute app 54992   51,552 MiB
    gpu 3   0 %   59,149 MiB      compute app 54993   59,140 MiB

Memory identical across all 20 samples, one compute app per worker, utilization 0 percent
throughout — while a different tick on the same phase read 52 and 70 percent.

So the phase is **GPU-RESIDENT but UTILIZATION-SPARSE**: live CUDA contexts holding 38 to 59 GB,
computing in bursts. My original 0 MiB reading simply predated worker allocation.

## Why this matters to the surviving question

The one thing I said might survive was advisory tuning for heterogeneous phases. This signature is
the concrete discriminator that question needs:

    utilization 0 percent  AND  memory ~0 MiB  AND  no compute apps   -> genuinely no GPU work
    utilization 0 percent  AND  memory tens of GB  AND  compute apps  -> resident, between bursts

The poller's gpu-idle advisory fired on the SECOND shape, which is a false positive: a phase
holding 38 to 59 GB per GPU with a live compute app per worker is not an idle pod, whatever
instantaneous utilization says. Utilization alone cannot separate the two; memory plus compute-app
presence separates them cleanly and cheaply, from the same nvidia-smi call the poller already makes.

That is a much smaller and better-evidenced change than the task I originally filed, and unlike my
retracted premise it has a live demonstrated instance.

Recommendation unchanged otherwise: do not implement the realized-use verification as scoped in the
body. Either narrow to the discriminator above, or close. Still your planner's call.
